comparisons.peer_topic: Manufacturing Capacity, Yields, and Demand Forecasting Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces risks from inaccurate customer demand estimates and the inability to maintain appropriate manufacturing capacity and yields, which could result from insufficient expansion investments, overestimation of demand leading to excess capacity, or reduced yields from design or manufacturing issues.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Broadcom disclose that their reliance on owned manufacturing facilities with a higher fixed cost structure compared to a fabless model creates financial risk when utilization rates decline. QCOM states that lower capacity levels result in lower gross profit because fixed costs continue to be incurred. Broadcom similarly warns that if it overestimates demand, 'excess capacity and fixed costs at these facilities will not be fully absorbed, which could adversely affect our results of operations.' Both identify the mechanical link between fixed cost burden and demand-driven utilization drops as a key risk to profitability.

sentences.text: Our manufacturing facilities are characterized by a higher portion of fixed costs relative to a fabless model.

We may be faced with a decline in the utilization rates of our manufacturing facilities due to decreases in demand for our products, including in less favorable industry or macroeconomic environments, or due to our failure to win and/or retain designs with OEMs. As a result, from time to time our manufacturing facilities operate at lower capacity levels, while the fixed costs associated with such facilities continue to be incurred, resulting in lower gross profit.

Conversely, if we overestimate customer demand, we would experience excess capacity and fixed costs at these facilities will not be fully absorbed, which could adversely affect our results of operations.

comparisons.peer_summary: Process technology and manufacturing investments require capital expenditures above historical levels due to high-tech fabrication facilities and EUV lithography costs. High fixed costs expose gross margin and operating income to demand decreases, leading to potential write-offs, impairments, such as the $3.1 billion charge recorded in Q3 2024 related to the Intel 7 node.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and Intel both highlight that ownership of high-tech fabrication facilities results in a high fixed cost structure that disproportionately affects gross margins and operating income when demand decreases. QCOM notes that fixed costs continue to be incurred even at lower capacity, resulting in lower gross profit. Intel elaborates that its 'high fixed cost structure' is difficult to reduce quickly and that if demand decreases, its gross margin and operating income can be 'disproportionately affected' due to these fixed costs, potentially leading to write-offs.

sentences.text: Our manufacturing facilities are characterized by a higher portion of fixed costs relative to a fabless model.

We may be faced with a decline in the utilization rates of our manufacturing facilities due to decreases in demand for our products, including in less favorable industry or macroeconomic environments, or due to our failure to win and/or retain designs with OEMs. As a result, from time to time our manufacturing facilities operate at lower capacity levels, while the fixed costs associated with such facilities continue to be incurred, resulting in lower gross profit.

Our ownership and operation of such high-tech fabrication facilities, and our need to build new and expand existing facilities in anticipation of future demand, has resulted and will continue to result in us incurring large capital outlays and high costs that are fixed or difficult to reduce in the short term.

To the extent customers are unwilling to pay prices to access the features that our process and product investments are expected to deliver, or if demand for our products, foundry capacity and assembly and test capacity decreases or we fail to forecast demand accurately, our gross margin and operating income can be disproportionately affected due to our high fixed cost structure, which is difficult to reduce quickly in response to lower demand and other unfavorable market factors.

comparisons.peer_summary: Output reductions or ramp delays caused by weak demand, oversupply, or supply chain disruptions can lead to production asset underutilization, increasing per-gigabit manufacturing costs and adversely affecting gross margins due to the fixed nature of many manufacturing costs.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM and Micron both disclose that a significant portion of their manufacturing costs are fixed, leading to adverse effects on gross margins when utilization or output declines due to weak demand or oversupply. QCOM explains that fixed costs continue to be incurred while facilities operate at lower capacity, lowering gross profit. Micron states that lower utilization and wafer output 'could result in higher inventory carrying costs, and have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our gross margins' specifically because many manufacturing costs are fixed and do not vary proportionally with production output.

sentences.text: Our manufacturing facilities are characterized by a higher portion of fixed costs relative to a fabless model.

We may be faced with a decline in the utilization rates of our manufacturing facilities due to decreases in demand for our products, including in less favorable industry or macroeconomic environments, or due to our failure to win and/or retain designs with OEMs. As a result, from time to time our manufacturing facilities operate at lower capacity levels, while the fixed costs associated with such facilities continue to be incurred, resulting in lower gross profit.
A significant portion of our manufacturing costs are fixed and do not vary proportionally with changes in production output.

As a result, lower utilization, lower wafer output, and corresponding increases in our per gigabit manufacturing costs could result in higher inventory carrying costs, and have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our gross margins, business, results of operations, or financial condition.
